supervisor_summary: DGX ($230.46) reconciles to a $216 horizon fair value ($215.97), $3 below the forecasters' mean ($219). The ladder stays at their mean (P(>=230) 0.44), and confidence is low. Round 2 settled three disagreements with primary evidence. JV minorities are worth ~$925M, not the $383M book (NCI has earned $50-54M a year). The horizon multiple is 17.0x, DGX's own 2021-25 median. PAMA is smaller than two agents assumed (Medicare CLFS is 8% of revenue per the 10-K), at 35% odds of cuts on schedule. The stock trades ~7% above fair value with a lame-duck PAMA binary by mid-December: a small diversifier at most, entered after Q3 (Oct 22) and the year-end extender package.
key_drivers: PAMA in the lame duck. Medicare CLFS is 8% of Quest's revenue (10-K). CMS's preliminary CY2027 rates are ~16% lower with a 15%/yr cap. Full cuts cost ~$0.85 of NTM EPS (~$14/share at 17x). The delay is on the Dec 31 health-extender list, which the lame duck usually renews; odds of cuts on schedule are 35%, and the expected deduction is $0.38.

The multiple. DGX trades at 19.2x FY27 consensus vs its own 2021-25 year-end median of 17.1x and LH at 15.9x. The adjusted-P/E gap to LH is partly definitional (GAAP EV/EBITDA 13.8x vs LH 14.2x, filing-based), but the 2026 sector re-rating happened with a 5.24% 10-year, so 17.0x, DGX's own median, is used.
Growth after Corewell and Fresenius lap in Q4 2026. Ex-deal volume grew +4.1% vs Labcorp's +1.8%. The company framework is 3-4% organic and 7-9% adjusted EPS growth.
JV partners' claim. NCI took $50-54M of earnings a year in 2023-25, and Corewell's 49% was added in 2026. At market value (~$925M) that is ~$8.3/share on the EV legs, not the $3.4 that book implies.
Q3 on Oct 22 and FY2027 guidance in early 2027. FY26 adjusted EPS guide is $11.05-11.25 (consensus $11.20); FY27 consensus is $12.03.
